narrative_purpose: Opens the chapter on its central strangeness: the largest thing in the sky never moves, so you tell time by the small sun crossing behind the fixed planet rather than by the planet itself.
subject: A wide Pandoran clearing in mid-afternoon. The enormous banded disc of Polyphemus hangs high and motionless, dominating the upper sky, its eye-storm slowly turning. The small bright yellow-white sun-star sits lower and off to one side of the planet, clearly the moving body, casting long raking amber shadows across the glowing forest floor.
scene: A living Pandoran clearing of luminous plants and tall alien trees, mid-afternoon, the air clear. The fixed planet looms; the low sun rakes the scene. A sense that the planet is a wall that simply stays put while light moves around it.
camera: Wide vista from ground level looking up and across the clearing, planet high in frame, sun lower - emphasising that the sun is the thing in motion.
light: Warm amber low sun raking from one side, long shadows; cool indigo sky; teal-cyan bioluminescent underglow from plants; thin warm rim on the planet.
palette: Void-indigo sky, warm amber raking light, teal-cyan plant glow, cream-rust planet bands.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, atmospheric depth, NOT a render.
detail_level: Crisp foreground clearing and plants, softer atmospheric planet, clean bright sun point.
composition: Polyphemus large in the upper third, small sun on a third line to its side, clearing and long shadows leading the eye across the lower two-thirds.
consistency_notes: Same Polyphemus as fig-00-cover (identical bands and eye-storm). Cool Pandora palette with bioluminescent underglow; planet reads as fixed, sun reads as moving.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no clock imagery, no orbit lines, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
